items.title: 'Trump has cost us': After midterm losses, MAGA asks if it's over
items.summary: "People are pissed off at Trump. Trump has cost us," he said, capturing a sentiment rippling through the president's Make America Great Again movement after the Republican Party's worst electoral defeat in decades. Across the coalition, some supporters who once viewed Trump as MAGA's greatest asset are beginning to question whether he has become its biggest liability.

items.title: Deepavali brings university breakthrough for orphaned son after mother's 16-year sacrifice
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: A single mother's 16-year sacrifice has culminated in a heartwarming Deepavali milestone, with her orphaned son finally securing a place at university after an appeal overturned a missed admission deadline. Dayvesh, who lost his father when he was two, grew up watching his mother work tirelessly to support their family while caring for his 84-year-old grandfather, Tata. That dream nearly slipped away a few months ago when Dayvesh's mobile phone broke down.

Fahmi said Malaysia had also made significant investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) since 2020. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial progress in 5G deployment, with the second network achieving 90 per cent coverage nine months ahead of schedule.

items.title: Malaysia to leverage AI and satellite networks for disaster preparedness
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 8 — Malaysia sees significant opportunities to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience, said Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil. He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies. Fahmi said Malaysia was placing greater emphasis on strengthening emergency telecommunications capabilities to ensure essential communications remained available when conventional networks were disrupted.

items.title: Melaka polls: MIC calls on Indian voters outside Melaka to return home
items.summary: MELAKA: State MIC has called on members of the Indian community living outside Melaka to return home to vote in the state election on Nov 14. Shanmugam, said every vote was important in determining the state's leadership and development direction over the next five years. "I believe the Indian community understands how important every vote is under the current circumstances.

items.title: Nations must decide own digital future, not be dictated to, says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 8— Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies, warning against a form of “technology colonialism” in which technologically advanced nations dictate how other countries develop and deploy their digital infrastructure. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development. Fahmi said Malaysia’s experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.

items.title: Police raid unlicensed KL entertainment outlet, detain 195 underage patrons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Police detained 195 underage teenagers and a premises manager in a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital after midnight last night. Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the teenagers detained in the operation, conducted at about 12.30 am, comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females. He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidate for Paya Rumput aims to ease voting process with personalised polling slips
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Paya Rumput state constituency Datuk Azman Abidin has introduced an initiative to help voters check their polling locations and channels ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14. Azman, popularly known as Tok Man, said he and his campaign team would assist voters in checking their polling details while campaigning, with the results printed on small slips and handed to them for reference. “Under this initiative, campaign workers only need to enter a voter’s identity card number to retrieve information on their polling location, including the school and assigned polling channel,” he told reporters after attending a courtesy visit and meet-and-greet programme with the Paya Rumput state constituency campaign machinery today.

items.title: 102 Melaka locations at risk of flooding during spring tides until Nov 17
items.summary: KOTA MELAKA: A total of 102 locations in Melaka have been identified as flood-risk areas following the spring tide phenomenon, which is expected to continue until Nov 17. He said preparations included round-the-clock flood monitoring across six main river basins, as well as continuous recording of rainfall and river water levels. "The early warning system is also being strengthened with the installation of 14 flood warning sirens and 10 monitoring cameras at strategic locations throughout Melaka," he said.

items.title: Penang Sentral offers round-the-clock waiting space for travellers, says Zairil
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Nov 8 — Penang Sentral, an integrated transport hub and major commercial development, provides a 24-hour waiting area on Level 1 at its stage bus platform, equipped with basic facilities for passengers. Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the facility was intended for passengers waiting for buses or their next connecting transport service. He said Penang Sentral was operated by Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and not the state government, adding that the waiting area was not meant to serve as accommodation or an overnight stay facility.

items.title: 195 underage patrons detained in raid on unlicensed Kuala Lumpur nightclub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 195 underage patrons and a premises manager during a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital shortly after midnight yesterday. Dang Wangi police chief assistant commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those detained comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females. He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.

items.title: Malaysia eyes satellite connectivity to strengthen disaster communications, says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia is looking to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and ensure communications remain available during emergencies, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said emerging technologies could complement conventional telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in remote and disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions might be required. He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of prolonged rain in four states until Wednesday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of continuous rain at the alert level for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu, until Wednesday. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan. In Pahang, the areas affected are Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while the warning covers the whole of Terengganu.

items.title: YNH Property races to plug RM6.8mil sukuk reserve gap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: YNH Property Bhd is working to plug a RM6.8 million shortfall in its sukuk reserve account as it steps up efforts to meet a RM170 million Islamic debt maturity due on Feb 26 next year. The property developer said it had accumulated RM54.4 million in the designated reserve account as at Oct 27, against the required balance of RM61.2 million for October. YNH Property said its immediate priorities were meeting monthly reserve-account requirements, accelerating collections from ongoing developments and completing asset disposals to fulfil its financial commitments.

items.title: Nations must not fall victim to 'technology colonialism', says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies and warned against "technology colonialism". Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development. Fahmi said Malaysia's experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.

items.title: Melaka plans five-year push to transform Kota Laksamana into state capital
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 —Kota Laksamana has the potential to become the new state capital of Melaka due to rapid development that can catalyse economic growth and transform the state's landscape, says Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf said the development plan also encompasses areas under the Straits of Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone (SM-WEZ), covering commercial, residential, healthcare and tourism sectors. Commenting on preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, Ab Rauf said the state government has stepped up disaster preparedness, including identifying 102 flood hotspots across the state.

items.title: Fahmi highlights Malaysia's early 5G coverage milestone at MWC Doha
items.summary: DOHA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has highlighted Malaysia's progress in expanding its 5G network, with the country's second network achieving 90 per cent coverage in October, nine months ahead of schedule. He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia's transition to a dual 5G network model aimed at strengthening competition, encouraging investment and improving telecommunications service quality. Fahmi said Malaysia had also invested significantly in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela) since 2020.

items.title: Japan man with 'grudge against society' stabs bookshop worker
items.summary: TOKYO: Japanese police arrested a 33-year-old man who admitted to stabbing a bookshop worker in Osaka on Sunday, a spokesman told AFP, adding that the suspect said he "held a grudge against society". The man, identified as Satoshi Okamoto, allegedly used a kitchen knife to stab the worker — who called police immediately afterwards — at a branch of national chain Maruzen & Junkudo in the heart of Japan's second-largest city. The suspect, who had remained inside the store until his arrest, admitted to the stabbing and told officers, "I held a grudge against society as a whole", according to the police spokesman, who briefed AFP on the customary condition of anonymity.

items.title: BN-Pakatan relationship unaffected by Najib pardon issue, says Zahid
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — Differences in political views and positions among parties in the Unity Government have not affected the smooth administration of the government, said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the working relationship between BN and Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the government remained good, with the administration of ministries and Cabinet meetings proceeding smoothly and professionally. Elaborating, the Deputy Prime Minister said differences in political approaches and positions among parties should be addressed maturely, particularly when political situations differ at the federal and state levels.

items.title: KTMB denies ownership of storage facility destroyed in Sepang fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has clarified that the storage facility destroyed in a fire at Desa Pinggiran Putra, Sepang, was not under its control or responsibility. Instead, KTMB said the facility, which housed equipment and security management assets, was managed and maintained by contractor X-Rail Systems. It was reported that an equipment storage facility believed to belong to KTMB was destroyed in a fire at Desa Pinggiran Putra, Sepang, at 10.42pm yesterday.

items.title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, 21 killed
items.summary: DAKAR: A boat carrying migrants sank off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 21 people in the latest tragedy along the dangerous Atlantic route from Africa to Europe, authorities said. Media reports said the boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis. Senegalese authorities said on Saturday that they had intercepted 142 migrants, including women and children, who were aboard a small boat attempting to reach Spain.

items.title: Flood-prone areas under close watch as wet weather looms in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 8 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department has stepped up patrols and monitoring in flash flood-prone areas throughout the state following forecasts of rain and thunderstorms until Tuesday. He said today’s forecast indicated rain in several areas in the morning, followed by thunderstorms in most areas in the afternoon and rain in most places at night. Mohamad Shoki said that on Tuesday, rain was forecast in several coastal areas in the morning, while conditions were expected to ease slightly in the afternoon and evening, although thunderstorms and rain were still forecast in some areas.

items.title: Continuous rain warning issued for east coast states, Sabah until Wednesday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an alert-level continuous rain warning for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu until Wednesday. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covered Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Baru, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan. In Sabah, continuous rain is forecast from tomorrow until Wednesday in Kudat and Sandakan, including Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan.

items.title: Malaysia stands in solidarity with Poland after shooting tragedy, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia stands in solidarity with the people of Poland and extends its condolences to the families of those killed in a shooting in Kraków, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar also expressed sadness over the tragedy, which claimed six lives and left several others injured, while wishing those affected a swift recovery. In the incident on Saturday afternoon, a gunman, reportedly inspired by far-right ideology killed six people, including a Briton, and injured many others in Kraków, Poland's second-largest city.

items.title: Anwar brings festive cheer to MIC-MIED Deepavali open house
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Deepavali open house organised by MIC and the Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning. Anwar spent time mingling with guests and dining with several political leaders, including former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong. Commenting on the event, Vigneswaran said the celebration showed that Malaysians could live in harmony and share in the joy of festivals throughout the year.

items.title: Najib's family still awaiting update on house arrest, says daughter
items.summary: "My family is very disappointed. We had made preparations to welcome my father home last Friday. Nooryana said she had also visited her father yesterday and that Najib was deeply disappointed with the latest developments concerning the implementation of house arrest.

items.title: Undocumented migrants pay syndicates up to RM15,000 to enter Malaysia
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Undocumented migrants smuggled into Malaysia through illegal jetties or sea routes are believed to pay syndicates between RM5,000 and RM15,000 each. Southeast Brigade General Operations Force commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the fees depended on the migrants' countries of origin and intended destinations. Radzi said at least seven illegal jetties along the Golok River were identified as entry points for undocumented migrants.

items.title: Was a BN convoy given priority? Two-car collision at Melaka traffic lights sparks questions
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — A Threads video is raising questions over whether traffic police gave a Barisan Nasional (BN) convoy priority at the time of a two-car accident at a junction on the Alor Gajah-Melaka Tengah-Jasin (AMJ) highway. On social media, someone remarked that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers and asked what had earned the group priority on the road. It noted that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers, and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.

items.title: No question of Negri Sembilan assembly being dissolved, says MB
items.summary: He said preparations for the tabling of the state Budget were finalised, with the state government now awaiting the official date for the sitting. There is no question of the state assembly being dissolved. He was responding to a question on the state government's preparations for the upcoming state assembly sitting.

items.title: Zahid cautions against further delays in implementing Najib's house arrest
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has cautioned against further delays in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest. His Majesty consented to Najib serving the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine for his SRC International case. The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.

items.title: Sabah expected to table biggest-ever budget on Dec 4
items.summary: He said the state government was still preparing the budget through consultation sessions, discussions and feedback from various quarters. Masidi said the preparations must take into account the state's revenue and capacity to generate income. Masidi said Sabah was awaiting the RM900 million special grant from the federal government.

items.title: Perak MMEA seizes vessel, probes unauthorised anchoring and reporting lapses
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 8 —The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Perak detained a cargo vessel suspected of violating the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952, about 4.3 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Jarak, near Lumut, yesterday. Its director, Maritime Captain Zainudin Mohd Zuki, said the Lumut Maritime Surveillance System radar detected the Gambian-registered vessel, prompting the Perak Maritime Headquarters Operations Centre to alert enforcement teams for inspection. He said the vessel had 21 crew members, including 11 Pakistanis, eight Iranians and two Indonesians.

items.title: AKPS detains 28-tonne buffalo meat shipment over import document irregularities
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) at Port Klang seized a consignment of buffalo meat, valued at RM413,728 and imported from India, at Port Klang on Friday (Nov 6). Port Klang AKPS commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said an inspection conducted by enforcement officers at 10.40am detected discrepancies between the halal certificate documents submitted and the information declared in the import permit. Following this, the entire consignment weighing 27,984 kilogrammes (kg) was seized for further investigation,” he said in a statement posted on the Port Klang AKPS Facebook page today.

items.title: Khairy: Chinese voters not afraid of 'blue wave'
items.summary: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin said he had never witnessed a situation in which BN component parties MCA and MIC felt uncomfortable with the presence or views of Pas ministers during cabinet meetings. He said differences in political views were normal and could be managed harmoniously without threatening the interests of any community. He said the results showed that cooperation with Pas did not necessarily diminish BN's support among non-Malay voters.

items.title: Melaka polls: Kota Laksamana could become new Melaka capital, say Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA: Kota Laksamana could become Melaka's new state capital under plans to develop a new economic corridor if Barisan Nasional wins the seat in the Melaka election. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal was part of the state government's plans to transform the area's development and economic landscape over the next five years. "I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the state capital.

items.title: Fake cops cheat retiree of RM179,490 in money laundering scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 —A 73-year-old retiree lost RM179,490 after falling victim to a Macau scam involving fraudsters posing as police officers and accusing him of money laundering and drug trafficking. Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the victim was initially contacted by two unidentified individuals claiming to be police officers, who instructed him to surrender his bank cards, cash and jewellery for investigation purposes. Hoo said the victim lodged a police report after realising he had been cheated.

items.title: Alliance Bank's BizSmart challenge down to 13 finalists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 13 homegrown businesses have earned their place in the finals of Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd's BizSmart Challenge Accelerator Edition 2026. Alliance Bank group chief executive officer Kellee Kam said the calibre of this year's finalists reflects the ambition, innovation and growing focus on sustainability among Malaysian entrepreneurs. They completed a four-day Accelerator Programme and Business Coaching, led by subject-matter experts from Alliance Bank, Alliance Islamic Bank, 1337 Ventures, Cradle Fund, Sunway iLabs, Sunway Malls and OneCredit, the challenge's credit reporting partner.

items.title: Retiree loses RM179,490 in Macau scam

items.title: Melaka lacks a real capital, says Ab Rauf, who wants Kota Laksamana to be it
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants to turn Kota Laksamana into Melaka’s state capital if it wins the seat in the coming state election, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. “God willing, I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the capital of Melaka,” he said at a campaign event at BN’s Kota Laksamana operations room here, attended by MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and BN candidate Melvin Chua Kew Wei. “So if we win Kota Laksamana, we will give the people of Kota Laksamana a centre that will become Melaka’s state capital,” he said.

items.title: Border security tightened in Kelantan amid migrant smuggling concerns
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Border enforcement agencies have stepped up security in Kelantan amid concerns over a rise in undocumented migrants entering the state by sea and land routes. An integrated operation involving several enforcement agencies, coordinated by the National Security Council (NSC) and led by the police, was launched on Nov 7 to tackle human trafficking, migrant smuggling and other cross-border criminal activities. "All agencies are working together to strengthen enforcement and prevent syndicates from exploiting the state's coastal areas and land border routes," the source said.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 11 states, federal territories
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast to hit 11 states and all three Federal Territories until 6 pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the alert covers Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Kinta, Kampar, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Batang Padang and Muallim. Meanwhile, in Sarawak, bad weather is forecast for Mukah (Dalat, Matu, Daro and Tanjung Manis), Sibu (Sibu), Bintulu (Tatau), Sri Aman (Pantu, Lingga and Sri Aman), Limbang, Miri (Marudi and Bario), Sarikei (Maradong), Kapit (Kapit) and Betong (Pusa and Betong).

items.title: Zahid brushes off talk of BN-PH rift over Najib house arrest issue
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Barisan Nasional (BN) has dismissed claims that the issue surrounding the conditional pardon and house arrest for Datuk Seri Najib Razak has caused a rift with Pakatan Harapan (PH). BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said coalitions continue to work professionally despite differing views, adding that Malaysia's political maturity was at an almost optimum level. Zahid was asked whether the issue surrounding Najib's conditional pardon and house arrest could further strain BN–PH ties in the unity government.

items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast to hit 11 states and all three Federal Territories until 6pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Kinta, Kampar, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Batang Padang and Muallim. items.title: Zahid's Turkiye visit advances US$10b trade ambition, defence and education cooperation
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has concluded his four-day working visit to Turkiye, with engagements focused on strengthening Malaysia-Turkiye ties in trade, defence, education and diplomacy. He later met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, with both sides discussing plans to increase bilateral trade from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030. Zahid also reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to its role as Asean-Turkiye relations coordinator.

items.title: Melaka first, Bersatu later: Perikatan chairman holds off on disciplinary action
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is putting off any decision on whether to discipline Bersatu until the Melaka state election is out of the way. PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the coalition had received complaints from its component parties about Bersatu’s conduct, Free Malaysia Today reported. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had earlier said the coalition would act against Bersatu for allegedly breaching its constitution, including by contesting against PN in the Negeri Sembilan polls.

items.title: New Covid-19 strain PJ.2.1 may mimic cold or flu symptoms – WHO
items.summary: MOSCOW: Symptoms of the new Covid-19 strain PJ.2.1 may be similar to those of a cold or flu, and testing is necessary, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. The WHO's Russian office earlier said that the risk of the new coronavirus strain PJ.2.1 spreading globally was increasing. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: MB: No dissolution of Negeri Sembilan assembly, Budget sitting to go ahead
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 8 — The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly will not be allowed to dissolve, and efforts will be made to ensure that its sitting takes place as scheduled, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. There is no question of the state assembly being dissolved. He was responding to a question on the state government’s preparations for the upcoming state assembly sitting.

items.title: Crew member missing as Indonesian water-bombing helicopter crashes [WATCH]
items.summary: JAKARTA: A helicopter battling Indonesian wildfires crashed into a river on Sunday while scooping up water, an official told AFP, with two crew members rescued and one still missing. Two Australian nationals survived Sunday's incident and were "safe", said Berton Panjaitan, a spokesman for the National Disaster Mitigation Agency, while the third crew member, an Indonesian, remained unaccounted for. Dramatic video footage showed the firefighting helicopter being slowly dragged downwards after filling its bucket from the Barito River, eventually plunging nose-first into the water.

items.title: ‘Mandatory’: Khairy tells Umno and BN voters to back PAS in Bukit Katil
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Fewer than seven months after Umno formally welcomed him back, Khairy Jamaluddin is on the Melaka campaign trail telling Barisan Nasional (BN) supporters to vote for a PAS candidate. The former Umno Youth chief said BN voters in Bukit Katil must back the PAS candidate there under the electoral understanding between the two sides, the New Straits Times reported today. “Send word to our friends, for example in Bukit Katil, because there is a PAS candidate there and we did not field a BN candidate,” he was quoted saying at a campaign stop in Duyong.

items.title: Nearly 3,000 guests, one cake: Anwar joins MIC’s Deepavali celebration in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Deepavali open house organised by MIC and the Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning here. Anwar spent time mingling with guests and dining with several political leaders, including former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong. items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Despite the relatively small Hindu population in Sabah and Sarawak, Deepavali celebrations today brought together people from diverse backgrounds, reflecting a strong spirit of unity. items.title: Prayers, reunions and open houses: Malaysia welcomes Deepavali
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — A festive mood filled towns and cities across the country as Hindus ushered in Deepavali today with prayers, temple visits, family reunions and gatherings with friends and neighbours. At the Sri Subramaniar Swamy Temple in Batu Caves near here, the grounds were already buzzing with activity early this morning as families in colourful traditional attire arrived to offer prayers. In PERAK, about 10,000 Hindus gathered at the Kallumalai Arulmigu Subramaniar Temple at Gunung Cheroh in Ipoh from as early as 6.30 am to offer prayers.

items.title: Wheel off, bumper wrecked: Chery says collision, not faulty parts to blame for viral NKVE car damage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Chery Auto Malaysia has moved to head off online speculation after images of a damaged Chery Tiggo Cross with a detached wheel and its axle spread on social media. The incident happened when the Chery car collided with a Perodua Myvi on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) yesterday. The incident comes about a month after the Road Transport Department temporarily suspended the vehicle type approval certificate for the Chery Omoda 5 following a separate incident in Johor Bahru.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected in Johor, Melaka and parts of three other states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Several areas in five states are forecast to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 3 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In Sabah, the affected areas are the West Coast and Interior, covering Keningau, Pensiangan, Tambunan and Sook; Kudat; Sandakan (Paitan, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan, Tongod and Telupid); and Tawau (Kalabakan and Tawau). Similar weather conditions are also forecast in several areas in Pahang, namely Temerloh, Pulau Tioman, Bera and Rompin, as well as in Negeri Sembilan, covering Jempol, Tampin, Seremban, Rembau and Kuala Pilah districts.

items.title: Ceilings leak at Seberang Jaya Hospital, no patients affected (VIDEO)
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 8 — Healthcare workers were seen holding umbrellas indoors at Seberang Jaya Hospital last night as rainwater poured through leaking ceilings and spread across flooded corridors, in video footage that has since gone viral. Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah confirmed that heavy rain and strong winds sent water seeping into several parts of the hospital, the New Straits Times reported today. “Most affected areas involved the hospital’s older building blocks, though several newer buildings were also impacted,” he was quoted as saying.

items.title: Health Ministry investigating claims of illness after consuming Gardenia products
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 8 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is awaiting laboratory analysis results and will conduct follow-up inspections at the Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd factory to verify compliance with the Food Act 1983 following complaints of alleged food poisoning involving the company’s products. In a statement today, MOH said preliminary investigations were underway into complaints circulating on social media and media reports of alleged food poisoning after consumption of Gardenia products, particularly Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot. “MOH has sought an explanation from Gardenia Bakeries (KL).

items.title: Melaka Polls: Adly calls for transparency on BN's manifesto promises
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) must provide detailed evidence to support its claim that it had fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka State Election in 2021, said Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari. Adly, who is defending the Bukit Katil seat in the 16th Melaka State Election, said transparency in presenting manifesto achievements was important to ensure that every commitment announced by the government could be assessed based on actual implementation outcomes, rather than merely percentage figures. He also said that based on a summary of the Auditor-General’s Report, the Melaka government suffered a deficit in 2024, with revenue of RM490 million against expenditure of RM519 million.

items.title: Kampung Murni A receives RM600,000 for hall, futsal court and youth skills training
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 8 — The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) has allocated RM600,000 to upgrade basic infrastructure and enhance youths' technical skills in Kampung Murni A under the 2026 Madani Adopted Village initiative. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the programme reflected the federal government's commitment to inclusive national development, including in rural areas. "The Madani Government introduced the Madani Adopted Village initiative based on a clear principle: national development must not leave rural and remote communities behind, while basic amenities and living standards in villages must be improved in a direct, tangible and immediate manner," he said.

items.title: ‘Negligence’: Johor Umno Youth wants Attorney General out over handling of Najib pardon
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 8 — A day after Istana Negara said Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon order was clear and unambiguous, Johor Umno Youth has turned its sights on the Attorney General (AG). The Johor wing chief Noor Azleen Ambros said the AG must answer for how the Pardons Board’s September 18 decision was carried out, The Star reported today. “Johor Umno Youth fully supports the firm stance taken by Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on the matter,” Noor Azleen was quoted as saying.

items.title: Melaka Polls: PH candidate Hakimin eyes education-employment hub for Ayer Molek
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Ayer Molek seat, Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar, wants to develop the constituency into an education and employment hub to create more job opportunities for residents if elected in the 16th Melaka state election. The 35-year-old Melaka Angkatan Muda Keadilan chief said Ayer Molek had considerable potential to attract higher education institutions, such as MARA colleges or polytechnics, as well as business establishments that could stimulate the local economy. Muhammad Hakimin, who holds a Bachelor of Administrative Science (Hons) from Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) and is a former Jasin Municipal Council member, said the two initiatives could bring significant long-term benefits to the Ayer Molek community.
